note: Two gate sets. 'regression' is enforced on every CI run and is pinned to the measured lexical baseline: its job is to catch a retrieval regression, not to certify quality. 'semantic_release' is enforced only when a run supplies captured on-device hits (--hits): it is the bar the on-device semantic feature must clear before it can ship as a default mode. Raising a bound to make a failing build pass is a process violation and requires a dated entry in docs/delivery/decision-log.md.

baseline_measured.comment: Lexical retrieval finds 1 in 5 labelled-relevant reviews on paraphrased questions. This is the measured problem the on-device semantic mode exists to solve, and it is the number any replacement must beat.

regression.rationale: Pinned at the measured lexical baseline with a small tolerance for floating-point summation. Passing this gate means retrieval has not got worse. It does NOT mean retrieval is good.

semantic_release.applies_when: a run supplies captured on-device hits via --hits
semantic_release.rationale: Agreed before the feature was measured, so the bar could not be set to whatever the model happened to produce. Recall 0.70 is a 3.5x improvement on the lexical baseline and is the point at which a product manager can trust the tool to surface most relevant evidence. The absent-topic bound is deliberately tight: a semantic retriever that invents relevance on topics the corpus does not contain is worse than no feature at all. Latency allows for on-device inference but excludes first-run model download.
